title: manual-procedure-record-v1
description: A SEALED, deterministic record of one manual reviewer-procedure (TC-00..TC-10) session run on a golden-box iteration, after the extension is installed. It is the cross-plane seam of the manual-procedure deterministic-record verification method: the LINUX plane produces this record (viewer monotonic counter + known-digit correlation + seal); the WIN plane's cross-iteration frame-diff consumes it. Once the on-screen counter is deterministically correlated to the viewer's emitted series the record is CLOSED: raw frames are DISCARDED, and only the time anchor + per-frame perceptual fingerprints + integrity hashes remain. Two distinct artifacts live here: (a) the counter series that CORRELATES to seal, and (b) the per-frame perceptual fingerprint used for cross-iteration visual-delta magnitude.

iteration.description: The golden-box iteration identity being verified (e.g. 'v1', 'v2', or a box tag). Cross-iteration diff pairs two records with different iteration values.

sessionId.description: Unique id for this capture session.

sealedAt.description: UTC timestamp when the record was correlated + sealed (raw frames discarded).

procedure.description: The manual reviewer procedure this session recorded.

cases.description: The ordered cases exercised, e.g. TC-00 .. TC-10.

anchor.description: The DETERMINISTIC time anchor + the correlation that CLOSED the record. Ground truth is the viewer's emitted monotonic counter series (we render it); the read series is the known-digit template read of the on-screen counter. The record only seals when they correlate.

source.description: The stopwatch is a monotonic counter surfaced by the extension viewer as plain high-contrast digits (NOT a colon-formatted OS clock, which OCR misreads per experiments/ocr-primitive-proof finding #3). It IS the mprr time-anchor, so the record is self-consistent.

counterStart.description: Viewer counter value at session start (the visible anchor).

counterEnd.description: Viewer counter value at session close.

readMethod.description: Linux-native deterministic known-digit / 7-seg template matcher (NOT fuzzy Windows.Media.Ocr). Template match => 100% deterministic read of glyphs we control.

matched.description: True iff every sampled read counter equals the expected viewer-emitted value. Sealing requires matched=true.

mismatches.description: Count of sampled frames where read != expected. Must be 0 to seal.

samples.description: Optional per-sample correlation proof (kept small; not the raw frame).

frames.description: One entry per retained frame, in capture order. RAW pixels are NOT here (discarded on seal) — only the counter read, a perceptual fingerprint (for cross-iteration visual-delta magnitude), and a cryptographic integrity hash of the original raw frame.

counter.description: Deterministic known-digit read of the viewer counter in this frame (the anchor for pairing across iterations).

perceptualFingerprint.description: Perceptual hash of the frame — supports MAGNITUDE comparison (Hamming distance) across iterations, unlike a cryptographic hash which is binary identical/not. THIS is what the cross-iteration frame-diff consumes.

fingerprintAlgo.description: The perceptual-fingerprint algorithm. Both planes MUST use the same algo to compare.

integrityHash.description: SHA-256 of the original raw frame bytes. The raw frame is discarded on seal; this hash proves it existed + was not altered, without retaining pixels.

seal.description: Proof the record is CLOSED/CLEARED: raw capture discarded, only anchor + fingerprints + hashes retained.

rawDiscarded.description: Raw frames are NOT retained. This is the privacy/storage property the operator asked for.

recordHash.description: SHA-256 over the ordered per-frame tuple (index, counter, perceptualFingerprint, integrityHash) — the tamper-evident id of the sealed record.
